sections.title: Definition & Foundations
sections.content: Perimetry measures the differential light sensitivity across the visual field. Kinetic perimetry (Goldmann) involves moving a stimulus of constant intensity toward the fixation point until detection (isopters). Static perimetry measures the threshold sensitivity at fixed locations by varying stimulus intensity (decibels, dB).

sections.title: Clinical Indications
content: Kinetic: Detecting peripheral contractions (e.g., Retinitis Pigmentosa, advanced Glaucoma).
Kinetic: Pediatric/Low-cognition patients (less demanding).
Static: Early detection of glaucomatous damage (RNFL thinning).
Static: Neuro-ophthalmology (Chiasmal/Retrochiasmal lesions).
Static: Longitudinal monitoring of VF index progression.

sections.title: Red Flags in Testing
content: High Fixation Losses (>20%): Invalidates reliability.
False Positives (>15%): Suggests 'trigger-happy' patient; elevates sensitivity.
False Negatives (>20%): Suggests inattention or advanced field loss.
Gaze Tracking Errors: Significant misalignment during testing.

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup Sequence
content: Step 1: Patient education and lens correction (near addition calculated per age).
Step 2: Trial frame alignment (check for rim artifacts).
Step 3: Fixation monitoring (Heijl-Krakau method for blind spot).
Step 4: Threshold strategy selection (SITA Fast vs. SITA Standard).
Step 5: Analysis of Global Indices (Mean Deviation, Pattern SD).

content.explanation: Fixation losses (check blind spot), False-positives (trigger-happy), False-negatives (inattention).

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Always adjust for age: Thresholds naturally decline with aging due to miosis and media opacities.
The 'Hill of Vision': Imagine the central fovea as the peak; sensitivity drops rapidly toward the periphery.
SITA (Swedish Interactive Threshold Algorithm) reduces test time by 50% compared to traditional Full Threshold.
Look for 'biconcave' patterns in bitemporal hemianopia (chiasmal pathology).
Artifacts: Eyelid ptosis or trial lens rims can create 'pseudoscotomas' in superior fields.

sections.title: --- Sub-topics from: Mastering Perimetry: Static, Kinetic, & SITA Strategies ---
sections.content: An essential clinical guide to visual field assessment, covering the physics of threshold perimetry, kinetic mapping, and the evolution of modern SITA testing algorithms.

sections.title: Definition & Purpose
sections.content: Perimetry measures the sensitivity of the retina to light stimuli across the visual field. It maps the 'island of vision in a sea of darkness'. Static perimetry (automated) assesses threshold at fixed locations, while kinetic perimetry moves stimuli from non-seeing to seeing areas.

sections.title: The SITA Revolution
content: SITA (Swedish Interactive Thresholding Algorithm): Uses mathematical models to predict thresholds.
SITA Standard: Traditional 24-2 or 30-2 protocols.
SITA Fast: Reduces testing time by ~50% with minimal loss in sensitivity.
SITA Faster: Further reduces time, removes blind spot monitoring to optimize fixation.
SITA Faster 24-2C: Adds 10 peripheral points specifically to detect glaucomatous damage in the central 10 degrees.

sections.title: Red Flags in Reliability
content: False Positives > 15%: Suggests 'trigger happy' patient (invalid).
False Negatives > 20%: Suggests fatigue or inattention.
Fixation Losses > 20%: Unreliable gaze tracking.
Gaze Tracking Graph: Look for spikes, indicating frequent ocular movements.

sections.title: Clinical Workflow: The Perimetry Process
content: Step 1: Proper refraction for age and testing distance (add +3.25D for near for 30cm).
Step 2: Trial frame or bowl-mounted lens correction (prevent rim artifacts).
Step 3: Patient instruction and practice 'dummy' run.
Step 4: Real-time gaze monitoring during testing.
Step 5: Analysis of Global Indices (MD, PSD, VFI).

content.explanation: G (Global Indices: MD/PSD), L (Losses/Fixation), A (Artifacts: Rim/Ptosis), D (Defect morphology: Arcuate/Nasal Step).

sections.title: Landmark Studies
content: OHTS (Ocular Hypertension Treatment Study): Utilized SAP (Standard Automated Perimetry) to define conversion to glaucoma.
EMGT (Early Manifest Glaucoma Trial): Established the 'Mean Deviation' (MD) as a primary metric for progression.
Comparison Studies: Confirmed that SITA-Faster provides comparable clinical utility to SITA-Standard while increasing patient satisfaction.
